notes.text: Elmer Söderblom is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 9 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Rutger McGroarty has taken his spot beside Connor Dewar and Blake Lizotte.
Evgeni Malkin is out, reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-six forward.

Bryan Rust is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 11 games. Tommy Novak has taken his spot beside Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell. That line has had 58% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 66:42 together, up from 43% with Rust.
Trevor van Riemsdyk returned in their last game after missing 15 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Ilya Solovyov has started killing penalties: on the ice for 43% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, up from 5% last season.
Nick Robertson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 20 games, up from 2% with his old team last season.
Lian Bichsel is out (lower body injury) and has missed the last 4 games.
Kyle Burroughs was added to the roster on Nov 15 and has played beside Trey Taylor.

story.head: The Stars come in hot
paras: The Penguins won the teams’ first meeting this season, 2-1 in a shootout in Pittsburgh on Oct 10. The Stars have won four straight, while the Penguins (7-12-2) lost 5-2 to St. Louis on Thursday. The Penguins played last night, and the Stars are rested. Going in, the Penguins are last in the Metropolitan (tied for 28th in the NHL) and the Stars second in the Central (tied for eighth).

The Penguins have played better than their record (.381) says: their chances are worth about .538, and their finishing has held them back. The Stars’ record (.682) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.602), largely because they’re 8-4 in one-goal games.

This season, the Stars have outscored teams 62-54, even though they’ve been outscored 40-39 at 5-on-5. On special teams, they’ve outscored teams 13-9, and no team creates more chances on the power play.

The Penguins sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (lowest), get more of their shots from in close than anyone (1st) and rarely throw hits (lowest). As for the Stars, they play slow, tight games (lowest) and take more penalties than they draw (32nd). They also block more shots than anyone (1st), and the Penguins’ knack for getting shots through meets a team that blocks a lot. Dallas has allowed 2.45 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. The Stars’ power play bites, but the Pens’ doesn’t.

Erik Karlsson (3 G / 16 A / 19 P in 21 GP) leads the Penguins in scoring, and Tommy Novak (8 G / 7 A / 15 P in 21 GP) has a team-high eight goals. For the Stars, Mikko Rantanen (10 G / 17 A / 27 P in 22 GP) leads the way in scoring. Jason Robertson (10 G / 16 A / 26 P in 22 GP) isn’t far behind, with seven points in his last five games.
Artūrs Šilovs (5-7-1 / .873 SV% in 13 GS) will likely start for Pittsburgh, and Jake Oettinger (12-4-1 / .901 SV% in 17 GS) for Dallas.
